item.title: Piton de la Fournaise enters new effusive phase inside Enclos Fouqué caldera, La Réunion
item.description: Piton de la Fournaise volcano on La Réunion entered a new eruptive phase at 19:42 LT (16:42 UTC) on January 18, 2026, after a strong seismic crisis and rapid ground deformation. The eruption is effusive, producing lava flows from fissures on the northern flank inside the Enclos Fouqué caldera. This is the first eruption at Piton de la Fournaise since August 2023. Source

item.title: Wave pattern in jet stream drives rare snow event across the Florida Panhandle
item.description: Rare snow fell across parts of Florida's Panhandle early on January 18, 2026, marking the second consecutive winter with measurable snowfall in the state. 2.3 mm (0.09 inches) of snow was recorded at Pensacola International Airport on the morning of January 18. Source

item.title: Rare S3 – Strong solar radiation storm in progress after X1.9 flare on January 18
item.description: A strong solar radiation storm (S3) is in progress after ≥10 MeV proton flux exceeded 1 000 pfu at 10:20 UTC on January 19, 2026. The event follows an X1.9 solar flare and full-halo coronal mass ejection that erupted on January 18. S3 - Strong solar radiation storms are relatively rare, occurring just a few times in one 11-year solar cycle. Source

item.title: Strong and shallow M6.0 earthquake hits southeast of Loyalty Islands, New Caledonia
item.description: A strong and shallow earthquake registered by the USGS as M6.0 hit southeast of Loyalty Islands, New Caledonia at 13:02 UTC on January 19, 2026. The agency is reporting a depth of 10 km (6.2 miles). EMSC is reporting the same magnitude and depth. Source

item.title: Nuclear-linked iodine-129 detected in the West Philippine Sea
item.description: Elevated concentrations of iodine-129 were detected in seawater samples collected recently from the West Philippine Sea during a nationwide marine radioisotope survey conducted by the University of the Philippines Marine Science Institute. The concentrations were higher than those measured in other Philippine marine areas, despite the Philippines having no active nuclear power plant or nuclear weapons program. Source

item.title: CME impact forecast early January 20 with G4 – Severe or higher storm risk and aurora as low as California
item.description: A G4 - Severe or greater geomagnetic storm is forecast for early January 20, 2026, as a full-halo coronal mass ejection from the January 18 X1.9 solar flare approaches Earth. If G4 conditions materialize, auroral activity is expected to expand significantly equatorward, with visibility possible as far south as Alabama and northern California. Source

item.title: Schools closed across Ukraine as power outages worsen extreme cold outbreak in Kyiv
item.description: An intense Arctic cold wave gripped Kyiv, Ukraine, in mid-January 2026, driving temperatures to -20°C (-4°F) amid an ongoing energy crisis. Large sections of the capital were left without heating or electricity after continued Russian strikes on the power grid, prompting some residents to temporarily leave unheated apartments and seek shelter in emergency warming centers. Schools across the country have been shut until February 1, due to the extreme conditions. Source

item.title: Winter storm warnings in effect across Great Lakes and Northeast U.S.
item.description: Heavy snow and strong winds continue across the Great Lakes and Northeast U.S. on January 19, 2026, with winter storm warnings and advisories in effect across the region. Snow accumulations are forecast to reach 15–-35 cm (6--14 inches) in Michigan and up to 120 cm (4 feet) in parts of northern New York. Source

item.title: Very rare S4 – Severe solar radiation storm in progress, G4 – Severe geomagnetic storm forecast
item.description: A G4 - Severe solar radiation storm is in progress after ≥10 MeV proton flux exceeded 10 000 pfu at 18:10 UTC on January 19, 2026, following the X1.9 solar flare on January 18. As the associated full-halo coronal mass ejection approaches Earth, forecasters warn that a G4 - Severe geomagnetic storm is likely early on January 20. Source

item.title: Woman killed, homes damaged as heavy rainfall and landslides strike New South Wales, Australia
item.description: Heavy rain and severe thunderstorms swept across New South Wales and southeast Queensland between Saturday and Monday, January 17 and 19, 2026, forcing evacuations around Sydney’s Narrabeen Lagoon and causing one death at Macquarie Pass. The storm system brought flash flooding, landslides, and dozens of rescues as the NSW State Emergency Service continued operations across inundated coastal suburbs. Source
